C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3.Summary: Run the rowless-archive payment survey the predecessor deferred, record what it proves, and take the findings window from one entry from full to hundreds of lines of headroom. The survey measured 54 archived bundles with no registry row in either sibling at commit 49b4ebb (76 archive directories, 48 distinct row names) and verified present-tree witnesses for payments by eight of them: C-CONTRACT-DEBT (F20, F29, F29.1), C-RECORDED-DEBT (F76, F71, F71.1, F77), C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY (F9.10, F31, F32), C-REPORT-HONESTY (F11, F11.2, F14, F15, F16), C-FLAG-HONESTY (F18), C-ESCALATION-HONESTY (F22), C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE (F13), C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT (F12) — 19 live findings, 699 live element lines under the shipped counting rule (newlineCount plus one per element). Eight historical rows land in live registry.xml, one per paying bundle, each payment witnessed by a symbol, a refuse path, or a file:line a reviewer can check without judgement; then a task runs scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire in the same execution wave, moving the eight rows and 19 findings to their retired siblings and stamping PaidBy. Then the bundle flushes the one staged entry F204 into findings.xml and decisions.xml — the index headroom admits exactly one entry and the freed findings room makes it free. Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30, D11; the record is this bundle's deliverable, so D30 is scoped, not skirted. Name searched at this commit: no archive directory and no row in either layer carries it.
C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3.Problem:
The findings window is one entry from full — base 7808 against ceiling 7846 at 49b4ebb, median element 35 lines — and the derivation cannot see most of the record's own history. 54 of 76 archived bundles have no registry row in either layer, so every finding they settled is unpayable by any path: the paid map mints 56 tokens at this commit and none of them names a live finding. C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 proved two payments out of that population and deliberately left the rest to a later charter. This bundle is that rest, scoped by measurement: the survey ran the predecessor's evidence rule over the rowless population and proved eight payers covering 19 still-live findings.
The yield is unevenly distributed and the survey says so honestly. Six of the eight payers announce their payments in their own spec prose — C-RECORDED-DEBT's Summary opens "Pay four recorded P1 debts in one bundle", C-CONTRACT-DEBT's names F29, F29.1 and F20, C-ESCALATION-HONESTY's says "Close F21 and F22", C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY's says "Close F9.10, F31, and F32", C-REPORT-HONESTY's lists F14/F15, F16 and F11/F11.2 among its deliverables, C-FLAG-HONESTY's says "fixing F18 as a class" — yet the shipped prose-mint pattern matches only the exact phrase "the paid finding(s)", which none of them contains, and the derivation reads no other sentence shape. The payments were made, witnessed in the tree, and are invisible to the record that should be able to read them.
The move and any flush must be ordered as in the predecessor: the room the rows open exists only after --retire re-anchors the findings ceiling, and the close ceremony's move is structurally too late because it follows the archive git mv. D30 freezes the record for a bundle that measures it; this bundle deliberately writes the record — that is the deliverable, stated here so it is a scoped exception and not a silent breach.

The flush of exactly the one staged entry F204 — a scope decision, argued here rather than defaulted. The staged buffer holds one entry at this commit (measured: one anchor, f204). The index admits it: decisions.xml base 339 against ceiling 341 leaves headroom 2, and one Entry line lands at 340. The findings room after the move is the freed 699 lines, so the entry's element size cannot breach the window at these numbers. Riding is worth more than staying staged: the record is one entry from full, the freed room is already paid for by this bundle's move, and leaving F204 staged buys nothing — the next bundle would need its own payment wave to flush it. The written findings root base comes from reading newlineCount back after the write, never from a projection; headroom is recomputed as ceiling minus the read-back base; the ceiling itself is untouched. A read-back base above the persisted ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling. The entry is selected by anchor id , never by position, and the element shape follows the landed rule the predecessor calibrated: buffer prose plus three wrapper lines.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record the retirement validator governs; no graph module is written, no src/ or scripts/ file is edited. Gates still run. Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Binding live rulings: D28, D28.1, D30, D11. D27: nothing in this bundle is approved unread; the payment set is repaired by evidence, never by editing a finding to fit it. The payment set is exactly the 19 findings named in Goals; no other token is paid by this bundle.

Payment evidence, the load-bearing rule, inherited from C-PAYMENT-RECORD and C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 and re-applied. Payments are proven first; the room is whatever falls out. Never select a payment because it frees the right number of lines. Sufficient, all of: (1) a present-tree witness — a symbol, a named test, a refuse path driven on the real CLI, or a file:line of the shipped behaviour that discharges the finding's defect, checkable by a reviewer without judgement; (2) the archived bundle that introduced that witness, with spec and plan status="applied"; (3) that bundle has no registry row in either sibling and its spec does not already mint the payment by prose, so the row is the only route; (4) the finding is still live. Insufficient, each refused: a bundle name or charter topic that merely sounds related; the finding's own discharge sentence without a tree check — a finding is never evidence of present state; sharing a file with a paid finding; a dated claim cited as present state; a spec claim of payment without the tree witness (six of the eight accepted payers announce their payments in prose, and prose alone refused none of them — the tree check is what admits each). Candidates examined and refused for this bundle, with the check that refused them: F21 — the renamed signature-budget mechanism exists (the predecessor's check, carried forward unchanged); F63 — the bundle's response is a design decision (one renderer, two emissions) whose discharge of the skill-text half cannot be checked without judgement; F41 and F35.1 — subject overlap with C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE only, no witness derived; F3 and F5.1 — the reject-don't-filter conversion shipped, but neither finding's separator or declaration defect is shown discharged by it; F137, F150, F155, F157 and F90 — not live (retired with PaidBy naming rows that exist). If the survey had proved fewer payers than the flush needed, the bundle would say so and stop; the honest yield is stated in Problem and it is enough.

Survey method, recorded so the number is reproducible. The population is every archive directory matching ^C-[A-Z0-9-]+$ with no Row name in either registry sibling (54 at 49b4ebb). Pass one: payment verbs within a clause of an F-token in each rowless bundle's spec.xml and plan.xml, read in context to separate payment claims from binding-constraint citations. Pass two: every rowless bundle Summary against every live finding Title for subject matches, each match chased to a witness or refused. Pass three: the derivation replicated — registry Pays and Closed-with tokens over both layers, plus the prose-mint pattern over every archived spec — confirming zero minted tokens are live, which is what makes every candidate row the only route. The 8-bundle, 19-finding yield is a verified floor: the 46 rowless bundles not named in Goals were examined by these passes and produced no provable witness at survey depth; the survey does not claim they contain none.

Retire ownership: a task runs the move. The close ceremony's --retire is an authority act performed after the archive git mv; it cannot open room for this bundle because every task, including any flush, precedes the archive. An authority act between tasks is refused for the same reason the predecessor argued: a record operation with no acceptance criterion, no evidence trail, and writes outside any plan-declared scope is silent by construction, whoever performs it. A task performing the move deliberately — declared in the plan, scoped by its write scope, verified by pre-move eligibility findings and post-move validation green with re-derived roots — is the operator use C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2 explicitly preserved. The operation is the deliverable, performed once, verified in both directions. Precedent: C-PAYMENT-RECORD's and C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2's Goal — "--retire is this bundle's move, not a follow-on" — executed in one execution wave, identically here, restated rather than cited as settled because the argument is load-bearing every time.

D30 scoped, not skirted. This bundle's purpose is to write the record: registry.xml (eight historical rows), findings.xml and decisions.xml (the F204 flush), and whatever the move writes — findings.xml, findings-retired.xml, registry-retired.xml, decisions.xml (Entry layer flips), and byte-identical rewrites of rulings.xml and rulings-retired.xml, which retireRecord writeFileSyncs on any successful move even when no decision is eligible. The freeze holds for the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files: no other dispatch touches the record while a record-writing task of this bundle is in flight, and no brief promises a frozen base across one. Findings raised while this bundle is open go to .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md (F205 onward), never into the record under edit. No scalar count of a record file appears in any Constraint; occupancy and wrap figures live in Assumptions and expire. Ceilings are rewritten only by the move and never raised; a flush that would exceed a persisted ceiling stops and reports.

Order, ceiling, and CI. The committed sequence is: (1) the eight historical rows in live registry.xml; (2) --retire in the same execution wave, before any commit validate:ci can see; (3) the flush of the one staged entry F204, writing first and reading newlineCount back for the findings root base (a projection is never a written root attribute); (4) validation exits 0. Live registry occupancy after insert and before the move is the pre-insert live row count plus eight, within the persisted registry ceiling (figures in Assumptions). A commit that holds the rows without the move is ineligible: validation reports registry-eligible-still-live and finding-eligible-still-live until the move runs. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. A second --retire after the flush is a byte-level no-op (moved = 0, early return before any write), the predecessor's fixture result, re-probed at close by AC-PAYMENT-SET's invariance.
